cyst kidney: well-defined, round or oval hypodense lesion with smooth borders
homogeneous low attenuation close to water density (0–20 HU)
no internal enhancement after contrast administration
absence of internal septations, nodules, or calcifications in simple cysts
clear demarcation from the surrounding renal parenchyma
thin, imperceptible wall with no irregularities
usually solitary but may be multiple in cases of polycystic kidney disease
no evidence of solid components or vascularity
non-distortion of renal contour unless large in size
unchanged in different contrast phases, supporting benign nature
kidney stone: hyperdense focus with high attenuation (>200 HU) within the collecting system
small, sharply marginated structure often in the calyces or renal pelvis
no associated soft-tissue mass or enhancement
may cause obstruction with hydronephrosis in larger or impacted stones
posterior acoustic shadowing on correlative ultrasound
non-enhancing and stable in pre- and post-contrast scans
no significant perinephric fat stranding unless complicated
common locations include ureteropelvic junction and calyceal fornix
may be associated with calcified debris in staghorn calculi
not associated with parenchymal distortion unless chronic
kidney tumor: solid or complex mass with irregular or lobulated borders
heterogeneous enhancement after contrast due to variable vascularity
mixed attenuation with necrotic, hemorrhagic, or calcified components
mass effect causing distortion or bulging of the renal contour
involvement of renal parenchyma with potential invasion into vessels
contrast enhancement pattern helps differentiate subtypes (e.g., RCC)
may show central necrosis or pseudocapsule
adjacent fat stranding or lymphadenopathy in advanced cases
often associated with displacement or distortion of the collecting system
clear cell tumors enhance more avidly compared to other subtypes
normal kidney: smooth, bean-shaped organ with homogeneous parenchymal texture
clear corticomedullary differentiation on contrast-enhanced images
normal renal contour without bulges or indentations
intact and symmetric renal sinus with visible fat content
normal collecting system with no signs of obstruction or filling defects
uniform enhancement of renal cortex in the arterial phase
no focal masses, cysts, or calcifications
renal pelvis and calyces appearing as low-density structures centrally
perirenal fat plane preserved and free of stranding
no vascular abnormalities or abnormal perfusion zones
